official.deadline_note: Country-specific: DFAT's opening and closing dates page lists the 2027-intake window as 1 February 2026 (09:00 AEDT) to 30 April 2026 (14:00 AEST) for most listed countries, including Bangladesh, the African country group, Bhutan and Brunei; other participating countries publish their own dates on the same table. The 2027 round has now closed and the country programme sites state applications reopen in early 2027.
official.application_cycle: study commencing 2027 (intake opened 1 February 2026, closed 30 April 2026)
official.status_note: Applications for the 2027 intake opened 1 February 2026 and closed 30 April 2026 at 14:00 AEST; the Australia Awards Bangladesh and South Asia & Mongolia programme pages state applications are now closed and will reopen in early 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: DFAT publishes the benefit as 'full tuition fees'.
benefits: return air travel - a single return, economy class airfare to and from Australia via the most direct route
establishment allowance - a once only payment as a contribution towards accommodation expenses, text books and study materials
Contribution to Living Expenses (CLE) - a fortnightly contribution to basic living expenses paid at a rate determined by the department
Introductory Academic Program (IAP) - a compulsory program prior to commencement of formal academic studies

Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) for the duration of the award (award holder only), Pre-course English (PCE) fees if deemed necessary, supplementary academic support, and a fieldwork allowance for compulsory research components
eligibility: Citizen of a participating country on the DFAT participating countries list; each bilateral programme sets its own eligibility requirements
Meet all eligibility requirements detailed in the Australia Awards Scholarships Policy Handbook (public DFAT pages point to the Handbook rather than restating full criteria)

Africa 2027 round published conditions: minimum 25 years of age on 1 February 2027; at least 5 years of post-graduate work experience in a field relative to the field of study; employed at time of applying; residing in and applying from country of citizenship unless working for an African Regional Organisation or on diplomatic mission
Not already holding or undertaking a master's degree or equivalent; already hold an undergraduate degree (Africa round wording; rules vary by country)

Not previously received a long-term Australia Award; Sri Lanka profile states applicants should not have received an Australian Government funded opportunity in the 24 months preceding the closing date
Sign a contract with the Commonwealth of Australia on acceptance and return to the home country for a minimum of two years after completing the scholarship
requirements: Meet the minimum English language proficiency published by the country programme (Africa round: IELTS 6.5 overall with no band less than 6.0, internet-based TOEFL at least 84 with minimum 21 in all subtests, or PTE Academic overall 58 with no communicative skill score less than 50)
Have an academic or professional background relevant to the proposed study program
English test scores must be valid at the intake date published in the country profile; candidates whose first language is English and who undertook their education in English may be excepted
Compile supporting documents as specified in the country profile (e.g., single PDFs named by document category, as the Vanuatu profile instructs)
Public sector employees may need official leave approval documents before departure (Sri Lanka profile)
documents: Online application via the Online Australia Awards Scholarships Information System (OASIS)
Academic transcripts and certificates (certified copies as specified in the country profile)
Employment references / referee reports (country pages publish CV and referee report templates, e.g., Bangladesh's application documentation page)
English proficiency test results (IELTS / TOEFL / PTE Academic)
Country profile documents published by the DFAT country page for the relevant intake
selection_criteria: Eligible applicants are assessed and shortlisted for interview (South Asia & Mongolia programme wording)
Academic or professional background relevant to the proposed study program
Applications must align with the priority areas of study identified by each bilateral country programme
Preference for development-related fields of study that contribute to the development needs of the partner country
coverage: Full tuition fees for the minimum period needed to complete the academic program specified by the Australian education institution, including preparatory training
Return economy class airfare via the most direct route
One-off establishment allowance on arrival (accommodation, text books, study materials)
Fortnightly Contribution to Living Expenses for basic living expenses
Overseas Student Health Cover for the duration of the award
Pre-course English fees where deemed necessary; Introductory Academic Program; supplementary academic support; fieldwork airfare for compulsory research components
application_method: Online via OASIS (Online Australia Awards Scholarships Information System) during the country-specific application window
official.application_route: Apply online through OASIS during your country's published application window; check the DFAT country profile page for the exact process and attachments before applying.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to citizens of eligible participating (developing) countries; applicants must be residing in and applying from their country of citizenship unless working for an African Regional Organisation or on a diplomatic mission for their home country (Africa round wording).
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is specifically for citizens of eligible developing countries, particularly in the Indo-Pacific region, to study in Australia.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Each bilateral country programme identifies priority areas of study that support its development objectives; country profiles publish the current priority fields.
official.duration: Offered for the minimum period necessary for the individual to complete the academic program specified by the Australian higher education institution, including any preparatory training.
official.description: Australia Awards Scholarships are long-term awards administered by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade that aim to contribute to the development needs of Australia's partner countries. They provide opportunities for people from developing countries, particularly in the Indo-Pacific region, to undertake full-time undergraduate or postgraduate study at participating Australian universities and TAFE institutions, developing skills and knowledge to drive change in their own countries.
official.region: Study in Australia; open to citizens of eligible developing countries (Indo-Pacific and African participating countries)
official.program_type: Long-term development scholarship administered by the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
official.english_requirement: Minimum English proficiency of at least IELTS 6.5 overall with no band less than 6.0 (internet-based TOEFL at least 84 with a minimum of 21 in all subtests, or PTE Academic overall 58 with no communicative skill score less than 50) for the 2027 Africa round; scores must be valid at the published intake date, with exceptions for native English speakers educated in English. Some country profiles may consider lower scores (e.g., IELTS 6.0 overall, no band less than 5.0 for Sri Lanka consideration) but awardees must reach IELTS 6.5-equivalent before commencing study.

verification.notes: Direct fetches to dfat.gov.au timed out repeatedly in this environment (main scholarship page, opening/closing dates page, how-to-apply page and intake PDFs all unreachable after multiple attempts), so values were taken from DFAT's own published pages as indexed, verbatim, and cross-checked across the main scholarship page plus the Africa, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Pakistan, Cambodia, Vanuatu and Maldives intake profiles on dfat.gov.au, corroborated by studyaustralia.gov.au; confidence marked low per the unreachable-page rule and a quick manual refresh of the main DFAT page could raise it. DFAT publishes no monetary figure for the fortnightly CLE ('a rate determined by the department'), so all amount fields are null rather than estimated.

applicant_utility.summary: Australia Awards Scholarships pay full tuition, return economy airfare, a one-off establishment allowance, a fortnightly living-expenses contribution and Overseas Student Health Cover, with Pre-course English and the Introductory Academic Program included - genuinely full funding, but not a signing bonus: acceptance comes with a Commonwealth contract that obliges you to return home for at least two years or repay the entire accrued cost of the scholarship. The 2027 intake ran 1 February to 30 April 2026 (14:00 AEST) for most countries including Bangladesh, so plan for the next window opening around February 2027 and use the months before it to lock in English tests and referee reports. DFAT deliberately does not publish the stipend rate, so treat the fortnightly CLE as a modest basic-living contribution rather than a salary - you will need your own buffer for setup costs, dependants and one-off expenses.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career professionals and strong recent graduates from participating countries whose proposed field matches their country programme's published priority areas and who can commit to returning home for two years after study.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country sits on the DFAT participating countries list and download that country's intake profile PDF - age, work-experience and priority-field rules differ per country
Shortlist courses that map to your country's published priority areas and to your own work background; relevance to the proposed study is a stated selection factor
Book IELTS/TOEFL/PTE early in the cycle: the threshold is 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 and scores must be valid at the intake date
Secure certified transcripts and certificates, and give referees several weeks to complete the report templates published on the country pages
Register on OASIS as soon as the window opens and submit well before the 14:00 AEST cut-off on closing day
Prepare for interview shortlisting - eligible applicants are assessed and shortlisted before interviews
common_rejection_risks: Proposed study that does not align with the country programme's priority areas or your professional background
English below threshold at the required date, or an expired test score
Already holding or undertaking a master's-equivalent qualification, or having received another long-term Australia Award recently (24-month rule in Sri Lanka wording)
Applying from outside your country of citizenship without the permitted exception
Missing certified copies, unused country templates, or a submission that misses the hard 14:00 AEST closing cut-off
Weak demonstrated link between the study and returning to drive development outcomes at home
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The award holder is covered, but dependants are not: OSHC covers the scholar only (excluding pre-existing conditions), family travel is typically restricted (Sri Lanka's profile permits family only after 6 months of study, at the scholar's own cost), and you should expect to fund personal setup items beyond the establishment allowance.
document_audit: Country pages require documents compiled as single PDFs by category with correctly named files - sloppy file organisation is an avoidable failure
Use the exact CV template and referee report template published on your country page rather than self-made versions
Certified copies of transcripts and certificates matter; uncertified scans are a common document trap
Check English test validity dates against the intake date before booking
alerts: Deadlines are country-specific and hard: the shared window closes 30 April at 14:00 AEST - treat February as the preparation month, not the start month
The two-year return-home condition is contractual: leaving Australia earlier triggers a debt for the total accrued cost of the scholarship
Public-sector applicants need employer leave approval documents before departure
DFAT publishes no stipend figure publicly - get the current CLE rate and conditions from the Policy Handbook and your country programme rather than from aggregator sites
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register and apply online via OASIS within your country's window with the country-page attachments; shortlisted applicants attend interview; the DFAT-managed country programme (with its managing contractor, e.g. Palladium for South Asia & Mongolia) runs selection and makes offers.

official.status_note: Nuffic's international programmes page lists 'NICHE/NFP' under 'Programmes previously managed by Nuffic'. Study in NL (Nuffic's own site) states: 'In 2024, the Orange Knowledge Programme ended. That means that there are no new application rounds for this programme.' The OKP was the NFP's successor scheme, and Nuffic's October 2024 news confirms the programme closed at the end of 2024.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Historic NFP published wording (NFP/MSP Grant Conditions, version 5, April 2016): the allowance is 'a contribution towards the costs of living, the costs of tuition fees, visa, travel, insurance and thesis research'.
benefits: An allowance as 'a contribution towards the costs of living, the costs of tuition fees, visa, travel, insurance and thesis research' (historic NFP/MSP Grant Conditions wording)
An NFP/MSP fellowship is 'intended to supplement the salary that the fellowship holder should continue to receive during the study period' - not a full-cost award
Where applicable, the fellowship holder is expected to cover the difference between actual costs and the amount of the personal NFP/MSP allowance
eligibility: The candidate must be a professional and a national of, and working and living in, one of the countries on the NFP country list valid at the time of application
The candidate must have a current employer's statement which complies with the format EP-Nuffic has provided, with all commitments endorsed
The candidate must have a government statement that meets the requirements of the country in which the employer is established (if applicable)
The candidate must have an official passport valid at least three months after the submission date of the registration form
The candidate must not receive more than one fellowship for courses/programmes that take place at the same time
requirements: Applications were submitted through the Dutch institution, which requests an NFP grant from Nuffic for candidates who comply with the eligibility criteria
All commitments in the employer's statement format must be endorsed by the employer
documents: Current employer's statement on the EP-Nuffic format
Government statement meeting the requirements of the employer's country (if applicable)
Official passport valid at least three months beyond the submission date
Course enrolment arranged with the Dutch institution, which submits the fellowship grant request to Nuffic
selection_criteria: The Dutch institution submits the grant request to Nuffic to subsidise individual fellowships for candidates who comply with the eligibility criteria
Only one fellowship per candidate for courses taking place at the same time is permitted
coverage: Historic allowance components, in the programme's own terms: costs of living, tuition fees, visa, travel, insurance and thesis research
application_method: Historic route: the candidate registered with the Dutch institution, which submitted the fellowship grant request to Nuffic; there is no open application route now that the programme is closed
official.application_route: No active route - the NFP is listed by Nuffic as a previously managed programme; current Nuffic-administered scholarships are the MENA Scholarship Programme, the NL Scholarship and Erasmus+.
official.citizenship_residency: Historic rule: the candidate must be a national of, and working and living in, one of the countries on the NFP country list valid at the time of application.
official.international_eligibility: Historic eligibility was limited to nationals of NFP country-list countries who were working and living there; the programme is now closed to new applicants.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Eligibility depended on the NFP country list valid at the time of application; priority areas were set per country programme.
official.description: The Netherlands Fellowship Programmes (NFP) was a scheme initiated and fully funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the budget for Development Cooperation and managed by Nuffic, giving professionals from NFP-listed countries a fellowship to study or train in the Netherlands. Nuffic now lists NICHE/NFP among its previously managed programmes, and the NFP's successor, the Orange Knowledge Programme, ended in 2024 with no new application rounds. Note: this catalogue title conflates the NFP with the Orange Tulip Scholarship (OTS), which is a separate Nuffic programme also listed as previously managed.
official.region: Study in the Netherlands; historic eligibility by NFP country list
official.program_type: Government-funded fellowship programme initiated by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs and managed by Nuffic (historic)

verification.notes: Live-fetched Nuffic and Study in NL (Nuffic's own domains) on 2026-10-10: Nuffic lists NICHE/NFP and OTS under previously managed programmes, and the Study in NL scholarship hub states the Orange Knowledge Programme ended in 2024 with no new application rounds. The stored URL /finances/ots-scholarships returns HTTP 404; the live hub is /finances/scholarships. No amounts are published for this closed programme, so all amount, deadline, English, duration and study-mode fields are null. Historic benefit and eligibility wording comes from the NFP/MSP Grant Conditions (version 5, April 2016) document published by EP-Nuffic and archived by Erasmus University Rotterdam (eur.nl), cited for the historic structure only.

applicant_utility.summary: Treat this catalogue row as closed, not as an opportunity: Nuffic lists the Netherlands Fellowship Programme among the programmes it previously manages, and the NFP's successor scheme, the Orange Knowledge Programme, ended in 2024 with no further rounds. The row also mislabels the scheme by pairing the NFP with the Orange Tulip Scholarship, a separate Nuffic programme that Nuffic also lists as previously managed - so any site promising 'NFP/OTS' funding for a current cycle is recycling expired information. If you are a mid-career professional the live Nuffic-administered routes are the MENA Scholarship Programme for nationals of the eleven listed MENA countries (fully funded short courses of 2-13 weeks, up to age 45, employer-backed), the NL Scholarship (a first-year grant at participating Dutch institutions) and Erasmus+.
applicant_utility.best_fit: No current applicants - the programme is closed; mid-career MENA-region professionals (MSP) and non-EEA students at participating Dutch institutions (NL Scholarship) are the working equivalents.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify programme status on Nuffic's international programmes page or Study in NL before investing time in any 'NFP' application - both list it as previously managed
If you are based in Algeria, Egypt, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, Oman, Sudan or Tunisia, check the MSP country page for priority themes and current rounds
If outside the MENA list, pivot to the NL Scholarship via your chosen Dutch institution's international office, and to Erasmus+ for mobility funding
Line up your employer early: the historic NFP required a signed employer statement on Nuffic's format, and MSP expects the employer to continue your salary and re-employ you afterwards
common_rejection_risks: Wasting a cycle applying to a closed programme that lists no application route
MSP applications that do not fit the published country approach - Study in NL states applicants who don't suit their country approach are not eligible
Employers with their own staff-development means (large national, commercial, donor or multilateral organisations) were excluded from the fellowship family's target group
Submitting more than one simultaneous fellowship application - only the last is considered and others are declared ineligible without notice
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Not applicable to a closed programme; for its current equivalents the NL Scholarship is a one-off first-year grant that does not replace full tuition, while MSP is advertised as a fully funded short course for eligible MENA professionals.
document_audit: Historic NFP applications hinged on the employer statement in Nuffic's exact format - employers that cannot endorse all commitments should not be asked to sign
MSP-style routes require your passport to be valid at least three months beyond the submission date
Keep evidence that your employer will continue salary and reintegrate you - it is a structural condition of this fellowship family, not a formality
alerts: Nuffic's October 2024 announcement states the Orange Knowledge Programme closed at the end of 2024 and that Nuffic phased out most activities outside Europe from 1 January 2025 - treat any newer 'global Nuffic fellowship' claim with suspicion
The catalogue title pairs two different Nuffic schemes (NFP and OTS); do not merge them when comparing options
MSP country participation can change - Sudan was excluded from the 2025 rounds due to circumstances, so check the current country list before relying on it
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: No submission route exists for the NFP; its live successor routes submit through the Dutch institution offering the course (for MSP) or through the institution's international office (for the NL Scholarship).
